newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London surges to new peak as rate fears wane.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London surges to new peak as rate fears wane.

text.p: London stocks surged to record levels for the second day running on Wednesday as fears receded of another interest rate increase but the rest of Europe was mixed.

On currency markets, worries about central bank intervention gnawed at the dollar, pulling it down by over a yen, its weakest level in more than a month. Sterling was calm after its exuberant jump in reaction to Tuesday's British interest rate hike.

London soared nearly one percent to 4,562.0, eclipsing the previous best intra-day peak set on Tuesday. Frankfurt fell 0.6 percent after hitting peaks yesterday but Paris, which performed poorly on Tuesday, perked up to show small gains.

The British bourse, Europe's biggest, was driven higher by weaker-than-expected output figures which calmed fears that the Bank of England might be tempted to push interest rates higher again in the near future.

"We're in the middle of a bull run and people are not going to want to trade against it aggressively," a trader said. But the pace of the climb was slower than the rapid movement seen on Tuesday amid euphoria over the new Labour government's decision to grant the Bank of England freedom to set interest rates without political interference.
Though finance minister Gordon Brown's reform of the British central bank was well received by the markets, some investors had started to become edgy about the direction of interest rates.
Behind the anxiety was the fact that sterling has risen 19 percent on a trade-weighted basis since August. The weak data showed that the rampant pound was hitting Britain's exporters.

News that manufacturing output and industrial production both fell 0.1 percent in March compared with expectations of a 0.3 percent rise helped to dampen speculation about another quick rise in interest rates.
European markets drew some comfort from Wall Street which chalked up its second record close in a row overnight though the rally was far more subdued than Monday's 143-point gain.

In Frankfurt, the fall in floor trade was seen as consolidation after Tuesday's record close. It was also reflecting yesterday's after-hours computerised deals on the IBIS index which ended down 0.5 percent after an unsteady start on Wall Street.
Trading volumes were thin, the market's mood edgy and activity generally subdued ahead of a national holiday on Thursday.
Paris pre-holiday trade, up 0.4 percent, was buoyed by a "reassuring" message from President Jacques Chirac who waded into the parliamentary election campaign to support the ruling conservatives.
The bourse was also underpinned by Wall Street, although traders said the U.S. influence had taken a back seat to political developments in France.

In currencies, the dollar fell against the yen as a market already jittery over intervention was spooked by a Japanese news report that Japan, the U.S. and Germany were exploring the possibility of selling dollars for yen.

"What's been said about intervention has always been that if the dollar's coming down the Bank of Japan will give it a helping hand," said Richard Hill, head of FX trading at Bank of America in London.
"People are nervous."
The dollar hit a session low of 124.92 yen as the market digested the report from Japanese news agency Kyodo though it picked up a little by midday.

The Bank of Japan declined to comment on the report, which quoted an international monetary source as saying the intervention move followed an accord -- reached at the recent G7 meeting -- to cooperate in the currency markets.
As the dollar weakened against the yen, it drifted down below 1.72 marks but was broadly stable.
Elsewhere, sterling was virtually unchanged after Tuesday's excitement , standing at $1.6375 and 2.8184 marks at midday versus $1.6372 and 2.8185 in late Europe yesterday.
STOCKS PRICES AT 1130 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 38. 2 points at 4,557.5.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 9.94 points at 2,661.87.
Frankfurt's DAX index was down 16.30 points at 3,551.98.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7184 marks compared with 1.7229 marks late in Europe on Tuesday. It was at 125.07 yen, compared to 126.44.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $340.65 an ounce, compared to Tuesday's close in London of $342.85. Silver was $4.73, down two cents.
